comparisons.peer_summary: Noninterest revenue increased 10% to $16.6 billion, driven by higher asset management fees from market levels and First Republic timing, increased card interchange and annual fees, and higher Home Lending production revenue including First Republic timing.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM report drivers for noninterest income/revenue growth, specifically citing card-related fees as a key contributor. BAC attributes an $85 million increase in Consumer Lending noninterest income primarily to 'higher card income' (bac_2024_7_P084_S003). Similarly, JPM reports that its Noninterest revenue (which includes consumer and business lines) was driven by 'higher card income, driven by higher net interchange reflecting increased debit and credit card sales volume, and higher annual fees' (jpm_2024_7_P153_S003). Both disclosures highlight card income/interchange as a positive revenue driver in 2024.
